content.text: Calypso is an unusual trick-taking game for 4 players in fixed partnerships, invented in Trinidad in the 1940s. Each player has their own personal trump suit (one player has Spades, another Hearts, etc.). Players build 'Calypsos' â€” complete sequences of A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2 in their own trump suit â€” by winning tricks and collecting the necessary cards. Completing a Calypso scores a major bonus.

Calypso was invented in Trinidad around the 1940s. It gained international attention in the 1950s following promotion by bridge authority Ely Culbertson who championed it as a potential rival to Contract Bridge.
4 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (208 cards total).
Each player receives 13 cards per deal. 4 deals per game.

items.text: Three-Player Calypso: Three players, each with own trump plus one suit shared as common trump. Rare variant.
